data.body:
Patchset 2 pushed (Gerrit 1878, commit 8ebad86, same Change-Id Ibd5eb6c). Addressed all 3 LLM-Review advisory findings from patchset 1:

1. (edge-cases) Lib force-parity: transition(force='') now treats empty string as NOT forcing, byte-identical to claim(force=''). Fix in _normalize_transition_force: result = force or None (a bare bypass is spelled with a non-empty reason). Test: test_empty_string_force_does_not_bypass_claim_or_transition.
2. (regression) NDJSON import close: reverted to a PLAIN (non-forcing) close. The old force=True was a no-op for an open->closed target (start-work bypass N/A; close gate keyed on unset force_close), so passing no force preserves exact origin/main behavior instead of newly bypassing the completion gate. Comment updated to explain.
3. (tests) force_close/force precedence: explicit unified force now WINS over the deprecated force_close alias when both are supplied (force_close only applies when force absent); the alias still warns. Test: test_force_wins_over_force_close_when_both_supplied.

Local: make lint (incl. complexity ratchet), make typecheck, and the affected suites all green with the venv; new suite now 9 tests.

Patchset 1 CI note: LLM-Review+1 (PASS) landed; Verified-1 was a SINGLE macOS py3.13 failure in tests/unit/test_code_review_gate_session.py::test_artifact_create_or_reuse_failure_never_fails_the_review -- a FileNotFoundError from a rebar-gate-snapshots tmp/build rename race in the code-review-gate SNAPSHOT machinery under xdist, an unrelated pre-existing macOS concurrency flake (all three Ubuntu pytest jobs passed). My diff does not touch that subsystem. Watching patchset 2 to see whether it recurs.
